title: Impact of Hospital Proximity on Mortality Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
• Method: Two-Stage Least Squares (IV).  
• Why: Care intensity (x) is likely endogenous (sicker patients both use more care and have higher mortality). Distance to the nearest hospital (z) is plausibly correlated with care intensity but, conditional on controls, should not affect mortality except through the intensity of care.  
• Key assumptions  
 1. Relevance – z is strongly correlated with x (first-stage F-stat ≳ 10).  
 2. Exclusion – z affects mortality only through care intensity (no direct effect once controls are included).  
 3. Independence – after conditioning on controls, z is as-good-as-random with respect to unobserved determinants of mortality.

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################
# Impact of Care Intensity on Mortality
# 2SLS with distance to hospital as instrument
###############################################

# 1. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
required <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
invisible(lapply(required, function(p) if (!require(p, character.only = TRUE)) install.packages(p)))
library(AER); library(sandwich); library(lmtest)

# 2. Load data --------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s67_data.csv")

# 3. Identify controls ------------------------------------------------------
# Keep everything except y, x, z as exogenous controls
ctrl_names <- setdiff(names(dat), c("y", "x", "z"))
ctrl_formula <- if (length(ctrl_names) > 0) paste("+", paste(ctrl_names, collapse = " + ")) else ""

# 4. First-stage ------------------------------------------------------------
fs_formula <- as.formula(paste("x ~ z", ctrl_formula))
fs <- lm(fs_formula, data = dat)
cat("\nFirst-stage results (x on z):\n")
print(coeftest(fs, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1")))

# Weak-instrument F-stat
fs_f <- waldtest(fs, . ~ . - z, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nKleibergen-Paap robust F-stat for relevance =", round(fs_f$F[2], 2), "\n")

# 5. 2SLS main specification -----------------------------------------------
iv_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ x", ctrl_formula, "| z", ctrl_formula))
iv_mod <- ivreg(iv_formula, data = dat)

# Robust (HC1) standard errors
iv_res <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nIV (2SLS) Results:\n")
print(iv_res["x", ])   # Show only coefficient of interest

# 6. OLS for comparison -----------------------------------------------------
ols_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ x", ctrl_formula))
ols_mod <- lm(ols_formula, data = dat)
cat("\nOLS Results (naïve):\n")
print(coeftest(ols_mod, vcov = vcovHC(ols_mod, type = "HC1"))["x", ])

# 7. Reduced form (y on z) --------------------------------------------------
rf <- lm(as.formula(paste("y ~ z", ctrl_formula)), data = dat)
cat("\nReduced-form (y on z):\n")
print(coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))["z", ])

# 8. Diagnostics ------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n—— Diagnostics ——\n")
print(summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics)

# 9. Clean numerical output -------------------------------------------------
cat("\n================================================\n")
cat("Care-intensity effect on mortality (IV point estimate):",
    round(iv_res["x", "Estimate"], 3),
    "\nRobust SE:", round(iv_res["x", "Std. Error"], 3),
    "\n================================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
• Sign: Negative. Greater care intensity should lower mortality, so the IV estimate of βₓ (effect of x on y) should be < 0.  
• Magnitude: Because the data are standardized, a one-unit increase in care intensity is expected to reduce the mortality index by roughly 0.4 – 0.8 standard-deviations (β̂ ≈ −0.5).  
• Interpretation: Living nearer to a hospital raises treatment intensity, which causally reduces mortality. Robustness checks (first-stage F-stat > 10, comparison with OLS, reduced form) should confirm instrument strength and the downward-bias of naïve OLS.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use distance to nearest hospital as an instrument for care intensity.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Proximity to a hospital significantly reduces mortality rates.
